record.name: Turkmenistan
record.summary: No qualifying institute or commitment identified. The communications minister announced a planned AI Development/Competence Centre at TurkmenTelecom for applied research, training and digital priorities. A draft national AI strategy was reviewed with UNDP in May 2026. The announcements give the centre no mandate to evaluate advanced models for their capabilities or behaviour risks.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches returned the draft-strategy process and the official January 2026 legal-framework announcement. The latter assigns future work on AI-use rules, agency responsibilities, standards and technical regulations. These are governance and adoption measures; neither it nor the existing applied-research/training-centre account establishes an AISI or institute-specific safety-evaluation study. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: The recorded tk query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Indexed results were sparse or noisy; the recorded language search does not establish complete coverage. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The existing UNDP account describes draft national AI-strategy consultation. The newly retrieved state-agency release records presidential approval of work on AI-use rules, government responsibilities, standards and technical regulations. Neither retrieved account specifies a national institute evaluating advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

record.notes: Read the State Radio Frequency Service March announcement in Turkmen, the Turkmengaz June account of the minister's speech, TurkmenTelecom's March strategy-workshop report, the UNDP May workshop announcement in English, and Russian official accounts of January AI legal-framework proposals and the February digital-economy programme. The ministerial centre announcement concerns research, professional training and sectoral AI pilots. Neither the centre nor the draft-strategy workshop specifies evaluation of advanced general-purpose models for their capabilities or behaviour risks; a general AI strategy study is not exploration of an AISI. The draft strategy itself was not retrieved. Previous broad-search source retained. A domestic transport-enterprise republication repeats workshop reporting; the substantive ministry-role account is UNDP's. An official report of 16 October 2026 says Turkmenistan proposed an international code for the peaceful use of AI in international relations and diplomacy; it is a diplomatic proposal, not a national law, strategy or institute.
